holder: ٱلَّذِينَ يَزْعُمُونَ أَنَّهُمْ ءَامَنُوا۟ — the people the addressee is told to look at; the same people are called ٱلْمُنَٰفِقِينَ in 4:61
proposition: that they have believed in what was sent down to you and what was sent down before you (أَنَّهُمْ ءَامَنُوا۟ بِمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ مِن قَبْلِكَ)
scope_note: يَزْعُمُونَ is affirmative, in the relative clause after ٱلَّذِينَ. The question أَلَمْ تَرَ governs تَرَ (the addressee's seeing), not the claiming, so I did not mark 'questioned'.
truth_evidence: Same verse, set against the claim: يُرِيدُونَ أَن يَتَحَاكَمُوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱلطَّٰغُوتِ وَقَدْ أُمِرُوٓا۟ أَن يَكْفُرُوا۟ بِهِۦ. 4:61 names them ٱلْمُنَٰفِقِينَ. 4:65, the text's own oath about them: فَلَا وَرَبِّكَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ حَتَّىٰ يُحَكِّمُوكَ.
unsure: attitude: يَزْعُمُونَ reports that they assert it. Whether they believe it of themselves is not stated; 4:63 says only يَعْلَمُ ٱللَّهُ مَا فِى قُلُوبِهِمْ. I recorded the assertion as 'held'
note: The proposition is about the holders themselves (their own faith), so 'grounds' fits poorly; the text is silent on what they rest the claim on.

holder: ٱلَّذِينَ ٱخْتَلَفُوا۟ فِيهِ (those who differed about him/it)
proposition: No clause is given. ٱلظَّنِّ stands as a noun with the article: conjecture about him/it (بِهِۦ, فِيهِ) — in context, about whether he was killed or crucified. What exactly they conjecture is not stated.
scope_note: ٱلظَّنِّ is governed by ٱتِّبَاعَ, the excepted term after إِلَّا. The negative مَا in مَا لَهُم بِهِۦ مِنْ عِلْمٍ governs their having knowledge; the exception leaves 'following conjecture' affirmed of them. So the negation does not fall on the attitude.
grounds_evidence: Same verse: مَا لَهُم بِهِۦ مِنْ عِلْمٍ (they have no knowledge of it), and before it لَفِى شَكٍّ مِّنْهُ. Earlier in the verse وَلَٰكِن شُبِّهَ لَهُمْ says how the matter was made to appear to 'them'; that is a cause of the appearance, not a ground the text credits.
unsure: proposition: the noun has no complement; the content of the conjecture is not stated, and those who 'differed' may hold different things

truth: left open because no single proposition is stated. If the conjecture is that he was killed, the text's own voice denies it in the same verse (وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ وَمَا صَلَبُوهُ ... وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ يَقِينًۢا) and the value would be 'false'
holder: لَهُم is taken as ٱلَّذِينَ ٱخْتَلَفُوا۟ فِيهِ, the nearest antecedent; it could reach back to the speakers of وَقَوْلِهِمْ إِنَّا قَتَلْنَا ٱلْمَسِيحَ
alternative: Read ٱلظَّنِّ as the supposition that he was killed or crucified: proposition 'that they killed him', truth 'false' (وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ وَمَا صَلَبُوهُ, same verse; بَل رَّفَعَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ, 4:158).
note: The verse sets ٱلظَّنِّ against عِلْمٍ and beside شَكٍّ. يَقِينًۢا at the end can attach to the denial ('they certainly did not kill him') or to the killing ('they did not kill him for certain'); I did not need to settle it.

holder: the subject of وَحَسِبُوٓا۟: بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ of 5:70 (the second blindness is narrowed to كَثِيرٌ مِّنْهُمْ)
proposition: that there would be no فِتْنَةٌ (أَلَّا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ)
scope_note: وَحَسِبُوٓا۟ is an affirmative past statement in the text's own voice. The negative inside أَلَّا belongs to the proposition, not to the verb.
unsure: truth: the verses read do not say that a فِتْنَةٌ came. The sequence (5:70 they denied and killed messengers; then فَعَمُوا۟ وَصَمُّوا۟ following on the supposing; then ثُمَّ تَابَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ) reads as blame for a mistaken security, which would be 'false', but that is implication and not statement
proposition: what فِتْنَةٌ covers here (a trial, a punishment) is not fixed by the verses
alternative: truth 'false' by implication from the blame in the context; nothing else changes.

holder: the plural 'you' of يَدْعُوكُمْ and وَتَظُنُّونَ: those who said أَءِذَا كُنَّا عِظَٰمًا وَرُفَٰتًا (17:49) and who will ask مَن يُعِيدُنَا and مَتَىٰ هُوَ (17:51)
proposition: that you tarried only a little (إِن لَّبِثْتُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا)
scope_note: قُلْ in 17:51 (قُلْ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَكُونَ قَرِيبًا) opens the answer; 17:52 continues it with يَوْمَ and the second person plural. وَتَظُنُّونَ is affirmative and set on a future day (يَوْمَ يَدْعُوكُمْ). إِن before لَّبِثْتُمْ is the negative that pairs with إِلَّا ('you did not tarry except a little'); it is inside the proposition and is not a condition.
unsure: reporter: no new قُلْ marks 17:52. I take it as continuing the instructed answer of 17:51 because the deniers are 'you' (كُمْ) as in the instructed lines, and not 'they' as in the text's own lines (فَسَيَقُولُونَ, فَسَيُنْغِضُونَ إِلَيْكَ). It could be the text turning to address them itself
alternative: reporter 'text' and scope 'plain', if 17:52 is the text's own address to the deniers.
note: The supposing is foretold for the day of the call, not reported as present. The verses read do not say how long they in fact tarried, so truth is open.

holder: the plural 'you' of زَعَمْتُم, those commanded ٱدْعُوا۟: the people the Prophet is told to address, who call on others apart from Him
proposition: that those (ٱلَّذِينَ) are [predicate not stated] apart from Him (مِّن دُونِهِۦ). The object of زَعَمْتُم is left out; the verse shows only that they are ones called upon who might be thought able to remove harm.
scope_note: قُلِ puts ٱدْعُوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُم مِّن دُونِهِۦ in the Prophet's mouth. زَعَمْتُم is an affirmative past in the relative clause after ٱلَّذِينَ; the imperative ٱدْعُوا۟ governs the calling, not the claiming.
truth_evidence: Same verse, within the instructed speech: فَلَا يَمْلِكُونَ كَشْفَ ٱلضُّرِّ عَنكُمْ وَلَا تَحْوِيلًا. Then 17:57, which has no second person and which I take as the text's own voice: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ يَبْتَغُونَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمُ ٱلْوَسِيلَةَ ... وَيَخَافُونَ عَذَابَهُۥٓ.
unsure: proposition: the predicate of the claim is elided; 'gods' or 'partners' is the usual supply and comes from memory, not from this verse
truth: 'false' holds if the claim is that they have power or standing apart from Him, which is what the verse and 17:57 deny; with the predicate unstated this is an inference
alternative: Take مِّن دُونِهِۦ with ٱدْعُوا۟ ('call, apart from Him, on those you claimed'): the claim then has no stated content at all, and truth would rest only on فَلَا يَمْلِكُونَ.
note: زَعَمْتُم reports that they asserted something; the verse does not speak of what they inwardly believe. I recorded the assertion as 'held'. Part of the truth evidence stands inside the speech the Prophet is told to say; I count words the text commands him to say as carrying the text's endorsement.

reporter_who: the subject of وَقَالُوا۟ in 17:90, those who say لَن نُّؤْمِنَ لَكَ; the nearest antecedent is أَكْثَرُ ٱلنَّاسِ in 17:89
holder: the singular 'you' of زَعَمْتَ: the one addressed by لَن نُّؤْمِنَ لَكَ, that is the Prophet, who is told to answer in 17:93 (قُلْ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّى)
proposition: that the sky would be made to fall on us in pieces (تُسْقِطَ ٱلسَّمَآءَ ... عَلَيْنَا كِسَفًا). The object of زَعَمْتَ is not spelled out; كَمَا points back to the falling of the sky.
scope_note: وَقَالُوا۟ (17:90) opens the speech, which runs to نَّقْرَؤُهُۥ in 17:93. زَعَمْتَ is an affirmative past inside the comparison clause كَمَا, attached to أَوْ تُسْقِطَ ٱلسَّمَآءَ, one of the demands governed by حَتَّىٰ after لَن نُّؤْمِنَ لَكَ. The demand is unfulfilled; the claiming is asserted by the speakers as already done.
unsure: attitude: that he claimed this is said only by the quoted speakers; the text's own voice in the verses read neither confirms nor denies that he said it
proposition: whether the claim attributed to him is that he would bring the sky down, that God would, or only that it could happen, is not fixed by كَمَا زَعَمْتَ
note: A warning about pieces of the sky falling stands elsewhere in the Quran; I know that from memory and did not use it. In the verses read, the reply قُلْ سُبْحَانَ رَبِّى هَلْ كُنتُ إِلَّا بَشَرًا رَّسُولًا (17:93) does not say whether the claim was made or whether its content is true. زَعَمْتَ reports an assertion; recorded as 'held'.

reporter_who: فِرْعَوْنُ, speaking to Moses (فَقَالَ لَهُۥ فِرْعَوْنُ)
scope_note: فَقَالَ لَهُۥ فِرْعَوْنُ introduces the speech. Inside it إِنِّى and the لَ of لَأَظُنُّكَ strengthen the statement; the verb is affirmative, first person, with كَ (Moses) as first object and مَسْحُورًا as second.
truth_evidence: Same verse, the text's own voice: وَلَقَدْ ءَاتَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ تِسْعَ ءَايَٰتٍۭ بَيِّنَٰتٍ — what Moses brought was given by God. Supported by the outcome in 17:103: فَأَغْرَقْنَٰهُ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥ جَمِيعًا. Moses's reply in 17:102 (لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَآ أَنزَلَ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِلَّا رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ) says the same, but it is quoted speech.
unsure: truth: the text has no sentence saying 'he was not bewitched'; 'false' rests on the text's own ءَاتَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ تِسْعَ ءَايَٰتٍۭ بَيِّنَٰتٍ and on the outcome in 17:103
attitude: recorded as 'held' because Pharaoh utters it with emphasis; Moses's reply لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ charges him with knowing otherwise, so whether he believes what he says is not settled
alternative: grounds 'expressly denied', if Moses's quoted لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ (17:102) is taken as the text's account of what Pharaoh knew.
note: That مَسْحُورًا means 'bewitched' (and not 'sorcerer') is from my knowledge of the word, not from these verses. While printing 17:45-57 for other entries I saw the same word used of the Prophet by ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ in 17:47; it did not decide anything here.

reporter_who: Moses: the subject of قَالَ, replying to Pharaoh and addressing him (يَٰفِرْعَوْنُ)
proposition: that you, Pharaoh, are مَثْبُورًا (ruined, doomed)
scope_note: قَالَ introduces the reply. Inside it وَإِنِّى and the لَ of لَأَظُنُّكَ strengthen the statement; the verb is affirmative, first person, with كَ (Pharaoh) as first object and مَثْبُورًا as second.
truth_evidence: 17:103, the text's own voice: فَأَغْرَقْنَٰهُ وَمَن مَّعَهُۥ جَمِيعًا.
grounds_evidence: Same verse, first half of Moses's reply: لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَآ أَنزَلَ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِلَّا رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ بَصَآئِرَ — Pharaoh knows the signs are from the Lord and still rejects them; وَإِنِّى لَأَظُنُّكَ follows on it with وَ.
unsure: grounds: the reply joins its two halves with وَ, not with a word for 'because'; taking the first half as what Moses relies on is my reading. If it is not, the value is 'not reported'
truth: 'true' depends on مَثْبُورًا meaning ruined or destroyed, which I supply from memory of the word; the drowning in 17:103 then confirms it
note: The wording mirrors Pharaoh's in 17:101 (إِنِّى لَأَظُنُّكَ يَٰمُوسَىٰ مَسْحُورًا / وَإِنِّى لَأَظُنُّكَ يَٰفِرْعَوْنُ مَثْبُورًا). I labelled each on its own evidence: the text's voice goes against the first and with the second.

holder: the plural 'you' of وَتَظُنُّونَ: those addressed in 33:9 as يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟, to whom the armies came (جَآءُوكُم)
proposition: No clause is given: suppositions about God (بِٱللَّهِ ٱلظُّنُونَا۠). The noun is plural and definite; its content is not stated in the verse.
scope_note: وَتَظُنُّونَ is affirmative, an imperfect set in the past by إِذْ / وَإِذْ ('when ... and you were supposing'). بِٱللَّهِ gives whom the supposing is about; ٱلظُّنُونَا۠ is its object.
unsure: proposition: the content of ٱلظُّنُونَا۠ is not stated; the plural suggests more than one supposition, perhaps differing between people

truth: open because no proposition is stated. Nearby the text reports two opposed sayings about God's promise: مَّا وَعَدَنَا ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥٓ إِلَّا غُرُورًا (33:12, ٱلْمُنَٰفِقُونَ) and هَٰذَا مَا وَعَدَنَا ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَصَدَقَ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ (33:22, ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ). If the suppositions are of both kinds, no single value fits
alternative: If ٱلظُّنُونَا۠ is read as only bad suppositions (that God's promise would fail), truth would be 'false' on وَصَدَقَ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ (33:22) and وَرَدَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ بِغَيْظِهِمْ (33:25).
note: Grouping: ٱلظُّنُونَا۠ is the noun of the same root standing as the object of وَتَظُنُّونَ, so the two words make one statement of one act of supposing. The frightening circumstances (زَاغَتِ ٱلْأَبْصَٰرُ وَبَلَغَتِ ٱلْقُلُوبُ ٱلْحَنَاجِرَ) are the occasion, not a ground the text says they relied on.

holder: the subject of يَحْسَبُونَ: those of 33:18-19, ٱلْمُعَوِّقِينَ مِنكُمْ وَٱلْقَآئِلِينَ لِإِخْوَٰنِهِمْ هَلُمَّ إِلَيْنَا, of whom the text says أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا۟
proposition: that the confederates have not gone (ٱلْأَحْزَابَ لَمْ يَذْهَبُوا۟)
scope_note: يَحْسَبُونَ is affirmative and not embedded under anything. The negative لَمْ governs يَذْهَبُوا۟ inside the proposition.
truth_evidence: Same verse: وَإِن يَأْتِ ٱلْأَحْزَابُ ('and if the confederates should come') treats them as no longer there. 33:25: وَرَدَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ بِغَيْظِهِمْ لَمْ يَنَالُوا۟ خَيْرًا. 33:9: فَأَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحًا وَجُنُودًا لَّمْ تَرَوْهَا.
note: The text does not use the words 'they have gone'; falsity rests on the three places cited and on taking ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ in 33:25 to be the same ٱلْأَحْزَابَ. The holders' fear is described in 33:19 but is not given as what they relied on.

proposition: No clause is given: his supposition about them (ظَنَّهُۥ, with عَلَيْهِمْ). The result clause فَٱتَّبَعُوهُ suggests the content: that they would follow him.
scope_note: ظَنَّهُۥ is a noun, the object of صَدَّقَ, with the pronoun هُۥ for Iblis. Nothing negates or questions it; لَقَدْ strengthens the statement that he made it come true.
truth_evidence: Same verse: وَلَقَدْ صَدَّقَ عَلَيْهِمْ إِبْلِيسُ ظَنَّهُۥ فَٱتَّبَعُوهُ — his supposition was made true on them and they followed him, إِلَّا فَرِيقًا مِّنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ.
unsure: proposition: the content of the supposition is not stated in this verse; 'that they would follow him' is inferred from فَٱتَّبَعُوهُ
proposition: whom عَلَيْهِمْ covers is not settled — the people of سَبَإٍ in 34:15-19, or people at large, given إِلَّا فَرِيقًا مِّنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ
note: Iblis's declared intention to mislead mankind is told in other suras; I know it from memory and it may colour the inferred content. Truth does not rest on it but on صَدَّقَ. With صَدَّقَ as printed (doubled د) Iblis is the one who makes the supposition true. 34:21 (وَمَا كَانَ لَهُۥ عَلَيْهِم مِّن سُلْطَٰنٍ) denies him authority over them; it does not speak of what his supposition rested on, so grounds is 'not reported' and not 'expressly denied'.

holder: the plural 'you' of زَعَمْتُم, those commanded ٱدْعُوا۟: the people the Prophet is told to address, who call on others apart from God
proposition: that those (ٱلَّذِينَ) are [predicate not stated] apart from God (مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ). The object of زَعَمْتُم is left out; the denials that follow (مِن شِرْكٍ, مِّن ظَهِيرٍ) suggest a claim that they share or help in His rule.
scope_note: قُلِ puts ٱدْعُوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ in the Prophet's mouth. زَعَمْتُم is an affirmative past in the relative clause after ٱلَّذِينَ; the imperative ٱدْعُوا۟ governs the calling, not the claiming.
truth_evidence: Same verse, within the instructed speech: لَا يَمْلِكُونَ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَلَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا لَهُمْ فِيهِمَا مِن شِرْكٍ وَمَا لَهُۥ مِنْهُم مِّن ظَهِيرٍ.
unsure: proposition: the predicate of the claim is elided; I infer it from the denials in the same verse, and 'gods' or 'partners' as the usual supply comes from memory
alternative: Take مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ with ٱدْعُوا۟ ('call, apart from God, on those you claimed'): the claim then has no stated content at all; truth would still be 'false' on the denials that follow.
note: زَعَمْتُم reports that they asserted something; the verse does not speak of what they inwardly believe. I recorded the assertion as 'held'. The denial stands inside the speech the Prophet is told to say; I count words the text commands him to say as carrying the text's endorsement.

proposition: that God will not bring out their rancours (أَن لَّن يُخْرِجَ ٱللَّهُ أَضْغَٰنَهُمْ)
scope_note: أَمْ opens a question and governs حَسِبَ: 'or did those in whose hearts is disease suppose ...?'. The verb itself is affirmative. لَّن negates يُخْرِجَ inside the proposition.
truth_evidence: 47:30, the text's own voice: وَلَوْ نَشَآءُ لَأَرَيْنَٰكَهُمْ فَلَعَرَفْتَهُم بِسِيمَٰهُمْ وَلَتَعْرِفَنَّهُمْ فِى لَحْنِ ٱلْقَوْلِ — they will be known. 47:31: وَنَبْلُوَا۟ أَخْبَارَكُمْ. Earlier, 47:26: وَٱللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ إِسْرَارَهُمْ.

holder: ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ (those who did wrong), on يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ
proposition: that what appeared to them from God would come to them. The thing is named only by مَا ('what they were not reckoning on'); its content is not stated.
scope_note: لَمْ negates يَكُونُوا۟ يَحْتَسِبُونَ ('they had not been reckoning'), inside the relative clause opened by مَا, which is the subject of وَبَدَا. I take وَبَدَا لَهُم as a statement of its own joined by وَ, not as part of the answer to لَوْ (the answer is لَٱفْتَدَوْا۟ بِهِۦ, marked by لَ), so I did not mark 'conditional'. The holders are a class named by description, which is the generic layer.
truth_evidence: Same verse: وَبَدَا لَهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَمْ يَكُونُوا۟ يَحْتَسِبُونَ — the thing they had not reckoned on did appear to them from God. 39:48 goes on: وَبَدَا لَهُمْ سَيِّـَٔاتُ مَا كَسَبُوا۟ وَحَاقَ بِهِم مَّا كَانُوا۟ بِهِۦ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ.
unsure: holder_kind: ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ is a class named by description, neither a particular group of an occasion nor all people; I chose 'generic'. 39:45 speaks of ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلْءَاخِرَةِ, who may be the people meant, which would make it 'specific'
scope: whether وَبَدَا لَهُم falls under لَوْ; if it does, add 'conditional'
proposition: the object of يَحْتَسِبُونَ is only مَا; what they failed to reckon on is not named
alternative: Read وَبَدَا لَهُم as continuing the supposed case under لَوْ: scope gains 'conditional' and truth would be 'open'.
note: That يَحْتَسِبُونَ means reckoning on or expecting something comes from my knowledge of the word, not from these verses. The verse describes an absence of expectation, not a held belief, so grounds is 'not applicable'. 39:46 is instructed speech addressed to God (قُلِ ٱللَّهُمَّ ... أَنتَ تَحْكُمُ); 39:47 speaks of God in the third person (مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ) and is not addressed to Him, so I took it as the text's own voice.
